suppliers.name: Connon Bros
suppliers.notes: Connon Oils is now part of Johnston Oils; Fuelsoft WebOrdering form (scraped via browser connector).

suppliers.name: Johnson Oils
suppliers.notes: Fuelsoft WebOrdering form (scraped via browser connector). Its website *is* its quote page here, unlike most: checked 2026-09-18, a plain fetch returns one form (`mainForm`) posting to OnlineQuote.aspx with seven selects and 141 mentions of postcode, so a human fills it in rather than reading a marketing page. That is what earns the order_page, and with it `order_channel: web`.

suppliers.name: Regency Oils
suppliers.notes: Fuelsoft WEBPLUS platform (scraped via browser connector).

suppliers.name: ValueOils
suppliers.notes: Priced by the ValueOils HTTP connector from the regional page's server-rendered `Total You Pay` table, which is why the record's website *is* that page rather than the marketing root: `website` is what the connector reads when its config names no `quote_url`, and it is also the page a human enters the Quick Quote form on. Discovery found this row under the page title `Aberdeenshire Heating Oil & Gas Oil`, so until 2026-09-24 every report named a page instead of the supplier; the register is where the name comes from now. A future repoint of this URL must move this row, not add one - `upsert_supplier` keys on the website, and the name refusal beside it exists to stop the quote history splitting across a twin.

suppliers.name: HomeFuels Direct
suppliers.notes: Priced by the HomeFuels HTTP connector from the live average in `#currentLivePrice`, which is why the record's website is the price page: the marketing root only links to it, and the connector reads the figure without signing in. Not asked by form or email - there is nothing to ask for, since the figure is public - so this record carries no `quote_request`, and `submit-requests` correctly does nothing with it. Repointing the website must move this row, not add one.

suppliers.name: Scottish Fuels
suppliers.notes: Priced through the signed-in Magento quote portal (`scottish_fuels_browser`, after `oilwatch login scottish_fuels`), and the replies `monitor-email` reads come from the same supplier. This is the one row whose `connector_config` matters to a human: the `order_page` is the quote portal, which is what earns it `order_channel: web`. Certas Energy is the same company, hence its entry in SUPPLIER_DOMAINS. Carrying the config here is not optional - `upsert_supplier` writes `connector_config_json` unconditionally, so a record without it would wipe the order page the live row already has.

suppliers.name: Rix
suppliers.notes: The Aberdeen depot, whose quote comes from the Rix quote tool (`rix_browser`) - browser-only, because the HTTP path is a contact-only connector that cannot price it. The form requires a phone number, which the connector now takes from the contact record rather than a drama number. Repointing the website must move this row, not add one.

suppliers.name: Gleaner Oils
suppliers.notes: The quote page is the wpforms form (id 1933), whose first field is a Receive a Quote / Place an Order choice; the winter-heating-oil page embeds the same form, so both take the same field numbers. Checked 2026-09-18: the page holds no price, so quote_by_request.

suppliers.name: Highland Fuels
suppliers.notes: Priced by its own `getoffers.php` XML API through the Highland Fuels connector, which needs the postcode; `highlandfuels.co.uk` is the domain the router matches, and the connector carries its own kerosene product code. This record said "Quote via form." until 2026-09-24 and that was wrong twice over: nothing here drives a form, and asking this supplier by form as well would be a second enquiry for a price the app already reads. `SUPPLIER_FORMS["highland_fuels"]` still exists as a hand-run fallback (`oilwatch submit-requests --suppliers highland_fuels`) for the day the API stops answering; it is deliberately not named in `quote_request`, so a normal `submit-requests` run leaves it alone.

suppliers.name: Fueltool
suppliers.notes: UK-average benchmark (scraped via HTTP). Not a local supplier. `kind` marks it as a figure rather than a company, so every row carries `kind: benchmark` and `order_channel: benchmark` and a consumer can refuse to present it as the winner without reading this sentence.

suppliers.name: Turriff Fuels
suppliers.notes: Website checked 2026-09-22: no quote form and no published price, so there is nothing to scrape and nothing to drive, hence `no_form`. The contact page carries rory@turriff-fuels.co.uk, so this supplier is asked by email; 01888 562706 is the number on the site, kept as contact data because the app never rings a supplier. That mail domain keeps a hyphen the website dropped, hence the matching entry in SUPPLIER_DOMAINS.

suppliers.name: Compass Fuels
suppliers.notes: Aberdeen depot (covers AB21). The homepage carries the 'Get Fuel Price' form (WordPress action compass_sector_lead), the same one on /aberdeen-fuel/; checked 2026-09-18. It asks for name, phone, email, postcode and litres and replies, so there is no price to read - hence quote_by_request rather than no_quote_page.

suppliers.name: Carnegie Fuels
suppliers.notes: East Scotland (Dunfermline to Fraserburgh). Online ordering is suspended by their own notice (carnegiefuels.co.uk/online-ordering-temporarily-unavailable/). Checked 2026-09-18: that page carries no form and no price, so there is no order_page to record, nothing to drive and no_quote_page is the honest reason - so it is asked by email at info@carnegiefuels.co.uk. 01356 648 648 is its listed number, kept as contact data.

suppliers.name: Nationwide Fuels
suppliers.notes: UK-wide. The quote form (quote[fullname]/quote[email]/quote[telephone]/quote[postcode]/quote[litres], the same fields on /fuel-products/kerosene/) posts to eforms.nationwidefuels.co.uk behind Cloudflare Turnstile and replies by email; checked 2026-09-18. No price to read, so quote_by_request.

suppliers.name: Crown Oil
suppliers.notes: UK-wide. The homepage quote form (quote[fullname] etc., the same fields on /products/kerosene/) posts to eforms.crownoil.co.uk behind Cloudflare Turnstile and replies by email; checked 2026-09-18. No price to read, so quote_by_request.

suppliers.name: Oilfast Insch
suppliers.notes: The Insch depot. The depot page is the quote page: two Gravity Forms (ids 10 and 2) behind reCAPTCHA, checked 2026-09-18, driven by oilwatch.form_submit; no published price, so quote_by_request. Depot line 01464 635999, general 03302 320 104.

suppliers.name: BoilerJuice
suppliers.notes: Broker/aggregator, deliberately not discovered (excluded_domains above lists boilerjuice.com). Quotes by email. Its browser connector signs in with the stored account and drives the journey's own form - postcode, volume, email, and the two required selects it used to leave on their placeholders; checked 2026-09-22, the browser refuses a submit while those are unanswered, so the page sat there unchanged and the run read as no_price_found. The quote then comes from the page's per-litre figure: the inclusive 'You Pay' option totals this note used to describe are no longer matched, and the service charge lives in those, so treat the number as the cheaper basis to compare on until they are read again. It earns its order_page the same way Johnson Oils does: checked 2026-09-18, the homepage's own buyNowQuoteForm posts to /uk/journeys/core/quote and says 'Get a quote', so there is a form on it rather than only a brochure.

suppliers.name: Brogan Fuels
suppliers.notes: RETIRED 2026-09-18: Brogan Fuels is part of Scottish Fuels, so it is not a supplier in its own right and no longer appears in any list, quote run or report. Kept as an inactive tombstone for two reasons: `init()` upserts on website, so simply dropping the entry would leave the live row active rather than retired, and the entry is where the retirement is recorded. brogans.co.uk is also in excluded_domains above, so discovery cannot re-add it.
